notes:
DG6 is an engineering delivery gate only. It grants no real business, Finance or IT approval and implies nothing about product gates G1-G6. Product G6 never implies DG7. The demo data and approvals in the evidence are synthetic and labelled as such.

This record replaces the round-4 BLOCKED decision (T-DG6-AUDIT-RG-R4, F-DG6-990). F-DG6-990 was repaired in T-DG6-BE-RG3 (60787d89f, D-239) and verified closed by domain-reviewer and code-security-reviewer (round 5) and by qa-verifier (rounds 6 and 7). It does not reproduce in this audit (0 served strings, against 24 at round 4). The record defect F-DG6-911/951 was fixed in e7cb240e7 and verified on the re-frozen candidate (D-240).

F-DG6-952 (Low, not mandatory: out-of-order history timestamps in the APPROVED DG0 and DG5 entries of stages.json; no product effect; the validator's history checks pass) is accepted as an observation by the user's decision (progress.md, 2026-11-12), by its reporter qa-verifier (round 6) and by the release-auditor (round 8, confirmed here). Owner: delivery-orchestrator. Rationale: rewriting the history of approved gates would change approved records with no change to any decision. Recommended follow-up: a non-decreasing-`at` check for new history entries, added through the tools/gates change process.

Until the runner writes this run's meta.json, validate --stage DG6 reports problems that concern only this in-flight run (14-validate-stage-DG6-final.log). The orchestrator also needs to set the stage state in stages.json.

Record observations O-R9-1 to O-R9-5 are listed in the audit record, each with its owner. Every audit condition holds, as listed in tests, and each was checked on its own evidence. No majority, score or deadline was used.
